blockers.title: Both RPM branches still begin from an undefined archive and neither proves that one archive supplied digest, verification, and manifest bytes
evidence: archiveAcquisition.selectionKey yields a unique installed rpmdb NEVRA. preferredApi.open then says rpmReadPackageFile on the unique rpmdb package matching that key, but names no archive pathname, repository/cache object, byte-returning rpmdb operation, or already-open descriptor from which rpmReadPackageFile obtains the original signed RPM bytes. The instruction to keep one descriptor starts after the missing acquisition step.

The fallback has the same gap: cliMaterializationIfNeeded.write says to write the unique rpmdb package blob, but no preceding operation produces such a blob. An installed rpmdb record and a NEVRA do not, within this contract, identify one retained archive byte sequence. Neither branch therefore defines the packagePayloadDigest input it later claims to hash.

The preferred branch names verify as the open choice 'rpmVerifySignatures / rpmts' with no one selected call or success output, and extract as an rpmfi walk of the same header. It never specifies an operation that consumes the held descriptor's cpio payload and hashes each regular-file payload member, so it does not construct authenticatedManifest from the same archive bytes as required by authenticatedManifest.builtFrom.

The CLI child tools still receive a pathname, not the held descriptor. A post-command fstatat/digest check proves only which inode is at the pathname after the child exits. A same-identity archive A can be replaced by signed archive B for the child's open and restored to A before revalidation; checksig and rpm2cpio can consume B while both after-checks observe A. 'keep the fd or reopen' is itself an or-choice and neither option binds the child's pathname open to identityRecord.

No rule reads the archive-internal NEVRA and requires equality to selectionKey and authenticityCore.payload.name/version. In the swap execution, signature success on B and extraction from B can therefore coexist with A's retained packagePayloadDigest and the selected installed NEVRA while every stated post-command identity check passes.
blockers.impact: RPM-family qualification is either non-executable because no archive bytes are acquired, or can mix digest/identity from A with signature verification and authenticatedManifest from B. A manifest unrelated to the signed package identity can then admit later file-backed objects or nominate the pathless kernel member.
blockers.requiredRepair: Define one exact archive source that returns immutable bytes or an already-open descriptor for the selected NEVRA, bind the archive's own header identity to selectionKey/authenticityCore, and use one selected descriptor-capable verification and payload-extraction procedure whose success values are closed. If a pathname-only tool remains, define an exclusion/descriptor handoff that proves the inode opened by each child is identityRecord; post-exit pathname revalidation alone is insufficient. Hash actual extracted regular-file bytes into authenticatedManifest and retain the source/consumption evidence in a lawful event field.

blockers.title: PCR-4 quote and log consistency does not prove that the authenticated kernel member is the code that executed
evidence: The acceptance predicate checks only that an AK signed PCR 4, that the quoted value replays from the supplied log, and that the log contains an EV_EFI_BOOT_SERVICES_APPLICATION digest equal to an authenticated package member. It does not compare the rest of the boot chain to approved measurements, verify Secure Boot or another enforcement policy, or name a DRTM/appraisal mechanism that makes measurement imply execution.

A quote authenticates the sequence of PCR extensions, not the semantic claim that a measured image was executed. An untrusted boot component can extend the approved member digest and record a matching event, then transfer control to different kernel bytes. The resulting event log reconstructs the quoted PCR 4, the approved digest equals authenticatedKernelMember.sha256, and all listed v26 checks pass although the running kernel is not that member.

kernelEvent's phrase 'whose digest is the loaded kernel image' is circular rather than an observation rule. EV_EFI_BOOT_SERVICES_APPLICATION also denotes boot applications generally; no event-data/device-path discriminant, trusted measuring component, or execution evidence establishes that the selected event is the executing kernel rather than another EFI application or a synthetic extension.

The quote nonce is deterministic SHA-256 of an unframed concatenation of an otherwise unencoded runIdentity and decimal observedAt. For example runIdentity 'r1' with observedAt 23 and runIdentity 'r12' with observedAt 3 both hash UTF-8 'r123'. observedAt is only a run-local monotonic integer, and no unpredictable verifier challenge or global runIdentity freshness is required, so a prior quote can be replayed for a different lawful association token.

The quote rule names PCR number 4 but no hash bank, TPMS_ATTEST/TPMT_SIGNATURE bytes, qualifiedSigner/AK-name check, PCR selection serialization, or exact AK certificate-store member join. measuredBootBind is extras-rejected, yet its quote object contains verification prose rather than the proof values needed to reproduce those checks.
blockers.impact: A machine can qualify a signed Linux OS-ABI package while executing a different kernel, defeating the central pathless authenticity bind. Deterministic ambiguous challenges additionally permit cross-run quote replay, and validators can select incompatible PCR banks or AK joins.
blockers.requiredRepair: Specify an end-to-end execution-rooted attestation profile: a trusted/enforced boot chain or DRTM/appraisal policy, exact kernel-event selection and measured-byte representation, approved boot-chain/reference policy, one PCR hash bank and replay algorithm, and a closed retained quote/AK/certificate join. Use an unpredictable verifier challenge bound through a length-prefixed canonical serialization to runIdentity, observedAt, subject, and signed carrier. The proof must exclude the execution in which approved bytes are merely extended before different bytes run.

shouldFix.title: materializedFileIdentity is required to be retained but has no lawful location in the closed event schema
evidence: cliMaterializationIfNeeded.retained names materializedFileIdentity {dir, name, dev, ino, size, sha256, associationToken}.

retainedEventSchema has no materializedFileIdentity member. Its only RPM authenticity-evidence slot is objectAuthenticityBindRecord, but the linux-file-backed tag is extrasRejected and declares openedObjectObservation, matchedManifestMember, packagePayloadDigest, and optional rpmHeaderIdentity only.

Emitting materializedFileIdentity beside the tag or inside it therefore has no declared closed form, while omitting it violates the explicit retained requirement. The associationToken and inode evidence cannot be reproduced from a conforming retained trace.
shouldFix.impact: Even a repaired runtime ceremony would have no canonical evidence record proving which materialized inode and digest were used. Independent validators can retain incompatible shapes or lose the claimed file-identity proof entirely.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Add a closed materializedFileIdentity field at one named event/tag location, require it exactly on the CLI RPM branch, forbid it on APT and descriptor-only RPM events, define field encodings and equality to identityRecord, and bind its associationToken, selected NEVRA, archive digest, and each consuming operation. Define an equivalent closed descriptor-consumption record for the preferred branch if that proof must also be retained.

shouldFix.title: rpmHeaderIdentity has two mutually exclusive extras-rejected schemas
evidence: The linux-file-backed tag defines rpmHeaderIdentity as the closed three-field record {sha256header, nevra, associationToken} and uses the latter two fields for the selected-NEVRA and same-event joins.
headerIdentity.retainedField independently defines that same rpmHeaderIdentity as the closed one-field record {sha256header}. Both definitions reject extras and neither supersedes the other.

A three-field event satisfies the tag definition but violates retainedField; a one-field event satisfies retainedField but violates the tag and cannot perform the claimed NEVRA/token bindings. Because the field is optional this does not itself false-allow an event, but the claimed retained header identity has no conforming present form.
shouldFix.impact: Producers and validators cannot agree on a canonical RPM retained record, and the v26 claim that header output is bound to the same NEVRA and event cannot be represented without violating another live rule.
shouldFix.requiredRepair: Choose one closed schema. Prefer {sha256header, nevra, associationToken}, update retainedField to that exact form, and retain the existing equalities to queryArgv output, archiveAcquisition.selectionKey, and openedObjectObservation.associationToken.

verdictBasis: REJECT: 2 blockers and 2 SHOULD-FIX findings. ACCEPT requires 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX.
conclusion: REJECT. v26 restores Linux pathless scope, removes global manifest-hash uniqueness, defines the EXTERNAL parent transform, and gates/binds RPM header metadata. It still does not acquire an RPM archive or prove that digest, verification, and extraction consume one byte sequence. Its PCR-4 ceremony proves only log/extend consistency, not execution of the allowlisted kernel, and its nonce is replayable. The claimed RPM retained records also have one missing location and one contradictory closed shape. DR-126 remains OPEN; Linux remains D-002 slice 1; no DR is marked SATISFIED, and no D-096 (A) grant, sealing, application, or implementation authority is created.
